Carry donor gauges' year-to-year departures onto an ungauged site

Source: R/wet_departure_carry.R
wet_departure_carry.Rd

Gives a site with no record of its own (or a short one) the departure of each year from normal, as the weighted mean of its donor gauges' departures. Each donor's departure is taken from its own baseline mean, so a donor's size does not matter, only how its years vary. The donors are the k gauges nearest the target in predictor space (easting and northing in km in BC Albers, EPSG:3005, and log drainage area, each divided by its standard deviation over stations), weighted by inverse distance as the monthly shares' and the daily shape's donors are. In a year a donor has no value, it is dropped and the remaining weights renormalised to sum to 1; a year no donor has is not returned.

Usage

wet_departure_carry(
  x,
  stations,
  target,
  k = 5,
  baseline = 1981:2010,
  min_baseline = 10
)

Arguments

x

Window statistics in wet_window_stats()'s long format (station_number, variable, period, year, value) for the donors and, if it has any record, the target. Each variable and period is carried on its own. Every donor chosen must have at least min_baseline years in baseline.

stations

data.frame(station_number, lon, lat, drainage_area_gross_km2), as from wet_station_select(), with a row for the target and every station in x.

target

The target's station number, or any id with a row in stations.

k

Number of donors.

baseline

Baseline years.

min_baseline

Fewest baseline years a donor needs, and the target needs for value.

Value

A data frame: station_number (the target), variable, period, year, anomaly (log, or days for *_cov_day), pct_normal, n_donors (present that year), donors ("station:weight" pairs used that year, separated by spaces) and value: the target's baseline mean carried by the anomaly, only where the target has its own baseline in x, else NA.

Details

A departure is a log ratio, log(value / baseline mean), reported also as percent of normal, 100 * (exp(anomaly) - 1), the scale cd::cd_anomaly() uses. A statistic named *_cov_day (a day of the window) departs in days instead, and has no percent of normal.

Examples

# Two donors share a wet year in 1990; the target, ungauged, gets it too
yrs <- 1975:2000
wet <- ifelse(yrs == 1990, 1.5, 1)
x <- data.frame(station_number = rep(c("D1", "D2"), each = length(yrs)),
                variable = "q_mean", period = "migration", year = rep(yrs, 2),
                value = c(20 * wet, 300 * wet))
st <- data.frame(station_number = c("D1", "D2", "T"), lon = c(-126.6, -127.8, -126.5),
                 lat = c(54.4, 55.1, 54.3), drainage_area_gross_km2 = c(2300, 900, 360))
a <- wet_departure_carry(x, st, "T", k = 2)
a[a$year %in% 1989:1991, c("year", "anomaly", "pct_normal", "donors")]
#>    year     anomaly pct_normal              donors
#> 15 1989 -0.02469261  -2.439024 D1:0.5770 D2:0.4230
#> 16 1990  0.38077250  46.341463 D1:0.5770 D2:0.4230
#> 17 1991 -0.02469261  -2.439024 D1:0.5770 D2:0.4230
